extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, petitioners, and patent practitioners participating in AIA proceedings before the PTAB
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for conducting AIA proceedings (inter partes review, post-grant review, covered business method review) before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, including motions to amend, preliminary responses, discovery, obviousness secondary considerations, and real-party-in-interest challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board guidance for motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: During a conference call before the patent owner files a motion to amend, the judges provide technical guidance to the patent owner and the petitioner regarding the motion. Parties may discuss issues regarding the proper scope of a motion to amend with the judges during the conference call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board cites prior decisions (MasterImage; Idle Free Systems; Int’l Flavors & Fragrances; Corning Optical; Riverbed Tech.; Reg Synthetic Fuels) as further guidance. Patent owners are advised to seek the Board’s guidance early if unclear about scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reissue applications to amend after final written decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office declines to propose a blanket rule stating that a reissue application can be used as a mechanism for amending claims after a final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue proceedings have additional requirements and cannot be the subject of a blanket change; issues remain governed by the separate reissue rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of persuasion for permitting consideration of motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner has a statutory right to file a motion to amend under 35 U.S.C. 316(d) and 326(d); there is no burden of persuasion for permitting the Board to consider a motion to amend because the Board must consider a motion that is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes the duty to consider a filed motion from the separate burdens of proof as to patentability when deciding whether substitute claims are patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curing minor defects in motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board deems it appropriate, the Board may allow a patent owner to cure minor defects in a motion to amend upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given time constraints, additional rounds of briefing may be incompatible with the schedule. Patent owners aware of defects should seek authorization to revise as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner estoppel under 37 CFR 42.73(d)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 42.73(d)(3), a patent applicant or owner is precluded from taking action inconsistent with an adverse judgment, including obtaining in any patent (1) a claim that is not patentably distinct from a finally refused or canceled claim; or (2) an amendment of a specification or drawing that was denied during the trial proceeding, but the provision does not apply to an application or patent that has a different written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule does not categorically preclude obtaining in another proceeding all claims that could have been filed; it precludes only claims not patentably distinct from a finally refused or canceled claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of motions to amend (filing with patent owner response)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office deems it most efficient for patent owners to file their motions to amend no later than the filing of the patent owner response, due to statutory one-year completion requirements for AIA proceedings (subject to limited extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may file motions to amend earlier in the proceeding if desired; the timing reflects efficiency and the statutory deadlines (see 37 CFR 42.121, 42.221).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim cancellation when patent owner concedes unpatentability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not adopt a rule requiring immediate cancellation when a patent owner concedes an existing claim's unpatentability and files a non-contingent motion to amend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board typically considers all papers together for the final written decision; parties may seek district court relief or request a conference call with the panel to seek earlier cancellation. Sanctions or disciplinary investigation may arise if a conceded claim is asserted in parallel litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of denied motion to amend into ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not permit converting a denied motion to amend into an ex parte reexamination of the substitute claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for ex parte reexamination differ from rules for motions to amend (compare 37 CFR 1.510(b) with 37 CFR 42.121, 42.221); a denied motion cannot be converted into an ex parte reexamination that bypasses reexamination requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowing new testimonial evidence with Patent Owner Preliminary Response
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office proposes to amend the rules to allow the patent owner to file new testimonial evidence with its preliminary response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To meet the three‑month statutory deadline for institution, there will be no right to cross‑examination of a declarant before institution; any factual dispute material to the institution decision will be resolved in favor of the petitioner solely for institution purposes. Cross‑examination is likely permitted only after institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of material factual disputes at institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Any factual dispute that is material to the institution decision will be resolved in favor of the petitioner solely for purposes of making a determination about whether to institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is proposed to preserve petitioner’s right to challenge statements made by patent owner declarants; petitioner may seek leave to file a reply to address testimonial evidence introduced in a preliminary response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner may seek leave to reply to preliminary response
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the patent owner may submit new testimonial evidence in a preliminary response, the Office proposes that a petitioner may seek leave to file a reply to that preliminary response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner will not have an automatic right to a reply but may request leave; the Director's regulations require providing the petitioner at least one opportunity to file written comments (see 35 U.S.C. 316(a)(13), 326(a)(12)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of 'new testimonial evidence' not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters sought clarification of the term 'new testimonial evidence' as used in 37 CFR 42.107(c); the Office states that additional clarification is not necessary in light of the proposed amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office believes existing rules and the proposed change suffice to guide parties on permitting testimonial evidence in preliminary responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garmin factors for additional discovery (adoption)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office adopts and will continue to apply the Garmin factors when deciding whether to grant a request for additional discovery in inter partes reviews, balancing meaningful discovery against preventing broad, expensive discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will apply Garmin on a case-by-case basis and plans to reflect this guidance in the Patent Trial Practice Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garmin Factor 1 — More than possibility/mere allegation
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere possibility of finding something useful, and mere allegation that something useful will be found, are insufficient; the requesting party should possess a threshold amount of evidence or reasoning tending to show beyond speculation that something useful will be uncovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Useful' means favorable in substantive value to the moving party's contention, not merely 'relevant' or 'admissible.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Garmin Factor 2 — Litigation positions and underlying basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Asking for the other party's litigation positions and the underlying basis for those positions is not necessarily in the interest of justice; there is a proper time and place for such presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine discovery rules (e.g., 37 CFR 42.51(b)(1)) permit cross‑examination of declarants; discovery of litigation strategy is generally disfavored absent specific justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garmin Factor 3 — Ability to generate equivalent information
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery is not in the interest of justice for information a party can reasonably figure out, generate, obtain, or assemble without a discovery request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should avoid seeking information that the requester could obtain by other reasonable means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garmin Factor 4 — Easily understandable instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery requests should be easily understandable; long, complex instructions (e.g., ten pages) are prima facie unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, concise requests protect against undue burden and ambiguity; requests lacking clarity may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garmin Factor 5 — Requests not overly burdensome
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board considers financial burden, burden on human resources, and burden on meeting the time schedule of the review; requests should be sensible and responsibly tailored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will consider the impact on the one‑year statutory schedule and may deny or narrow requests that would disrupt the schedule or impose undue cost or resource burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible application and non‑exhaustive nature of Garmin factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Garmin's list of factors is flexible and not exhaustive; the Office will consider other relevant factors such as whether the information is solely in the other party's possession, whether it has been produced in a related matter, and whether it relates to jurisdictional issues (35 U.S.C. 315 and 325).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office decides discovery disputes fact‑dependently and may consider suggested additional factors as subsumed under Garmin; parties may present different combinations of factors to support their requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold showing for moving party (no need for actual evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A moving party should present a threshold amount of evidence or reasoning tending to show beyond speculation that something useful will be uncovered, but the Office does not require the moving party to have actual evidence of the type being sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures against speculative fishing expeditions while allowing reasonable, well‑reasoned requests; a dissatisfied party may seek rehearing if the Office overlooked matters in denying discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery of petitioner's non‑obviousness evidence (commercial success)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to discover evidence of non‑obviousness held by the petitioner (e.g., commercial success evidence for a petitioner's product) will be evaluated under the Garmin factors and generally will be allowed only when narrowly tailored and necessary in the interest of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting discovery of a petitioner's product is rare because it can create mini‑trial issues and undermine efficient AIA trials; parties are encouraged to agree on initial disclosures and the Office will decide on a case‑by‑case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing of nexus for secondary considerations discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner seeking discovery of a petitioner's evidence of secondary considerations should present some showing of nexus between the claimed invention and the information sought; a conclusive showing is not required, but mere possibility or mere infringement contention is generally insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner should present threshold evidence or reasoning beyond speculation that useful evidence will be uncovered; evidence must address the possibility that success derived from features other than the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of focused interrogatories/productions for secondary considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree to limited, focused interrogatories and document requests related to secondary considerations; the Office declines to adopt a mandatory rule making such discovery available as of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 42.51(a)(1) and (b)(2) permit parties to agree to additional discovery even prior to institution; the Office encourages cooperation and will entertain case‑by‑case requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raising real party‑in‑interest/privity challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner will generally be permitted to raise a challenge regarding a real party‑in‑interest or privity at any time during a trial proceeding, although such challenges are preferably raised early (e.g., in the preliminary response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a late challenge reasonably could have been raised earlier, the Office will consider the impact of the delay (prejudice, unwarranted delay) on a case‑by‑case basis and may condition additional discovery or relief accordingly; Board practice permits seeking authority to take discovery or file a motion to challenge standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested disclosures for real party‑in‑interest issues (not mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters suggested requiring disclosure of joint defense agreements, indemnity agreements, identification of counsel in related litigation, parties participating in the preparation of the petition, and identification of parties funding the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office declines to impose such burdensome mandatory disclosure requirements and finds current practice appropriate for resolving real party‑in‑interest and privity issues efficiently; parties may, however, agree to provide such information or seek targeted discovery when justified.
